situation.text: Hoje você conhece Malik, de Milwaukee. Pedir combo e trocar acompanhamento.

pages.goal: Hoje você aprende a falar das refeições com o verbo have: have breakfast, have lunch, have dinner, como a lagarta faminta.
canDo: Say: Soon you’ll be a butterfly.

pages.hook: In a burger place in Milwaukee, you say your order, hear one question about a combo and move on. Learn how to order fast food without stress.

mythfact.s: A combo meal usually includes a main food, fries and a drink.
mythfact.why: A burger combo is typically a burger, fries and a drink in one price.

mythfact.s: In the USA, people always call a soft drink “cola”.
mythfact.why: Many say “soda”, and some regions say “pop” or the brand name.

mythfact.s: Milwaukee is in the state of Wisconsin.
mythfact.why: It is the biggest city in Wisconsin, on Lake Michigan.

mythfact.s: It is rude to say “No, thanks. That’s all.”
mythfact.why: It is a normal and polite way to end an order.

mythfact.s: “The Very Hungry Caterpillar” was written by Eric Carle.
mythfact.why: The picture book came out in 1969.

decode.q: How much more is the combo than the burger alone?

compare.br: In Brazil, a “combo” or “promoção” at a lanchonete is also common, and you may order at a counter or from an app.
compare.us: In the USA, the cashier usually asks “Do you want a combo?” and “Anything else?”.
compare.tip: Say “No, thanks. That’s all.” to finish your order.

pages.title: Reading quest — My burger day
text: I am in **Milwaukee**, and I am very hungry. It is like the story of The Very Hungry Caterpillar: today I want to eat a lot! My friend Gus takes me to a burger place.

The cashier, Malik, smiles. “**Welcome! What can I get you?**” I say, “**A cheeseburger, please.**” He asks, “**Do you want a combo?**” I am not sure, so I ask, “**What comes with it?**” “**Fries and a drink**,” he says.

That sounds good. “**OK. A combo, and a cola.**” “**Anything else?**” “**No, thanks. That’s all.**” Gus laughs because he wants lemonade and extra ketchup. The tray is full: a burger, fries and a cold drink.
“**Enjoy your burger!**” Malik says. I take a big bite. It is hot and tasty. Gus says, “**Let’s supersize it!**” but I say, “No, I feel full.” That is a good ending: not too much, not too little.
The caterpillar in the book becomes a butterfly after a big meal. I just became a very happy customer. Next time I will say, “I’m so hungry!” again, but maybe I will order a salad.
